data.narrative:
Deep Atomic is a pre-seed nuclear energy company founded by William G.J. Theron. The nuclear energy sector comprises a limited but active peer universe of 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private firms (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, Zephyr Fusion), totaling 8 comparable businesses across advanced fission and fusion segments.

The peer-median method is not applicable to Deep Atomic's valuation. A search across same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier filters identified zero same-stage peers, one adjacent-stage peer, and zero similar-valuation-tier peers—falling short of the minimum three datapoints required for statistical reliability. While the broader nuclear energy sector includes four peers, the heterogeneity of business models, technology maturity, and financing stages (ranging from public equities to various private rounds) precludes a meaningful median-based inference. An all-sector median would introduce substantial noise without anchoring to Deep Atomic's specific stage and capitalization profile.

Without sufficient comparable-company data at the pre-seed stage, this analysis cannot support a triangulated valuation range. The primary uncertainty stems from the scarcity of pre-seed nuclear technology financings in public records, limiting empirical benchmarking. Forward valuation work should consider: (i) expansion of the peer set to include early-stage fission or fusion companies outside the immediate nuclear sphere; (ii) venture capital check size norms for deep-tech hardware at pre-seed; or (iii) venture capital method approaches tied to downstream financing expectations and risk-adjusted returns.
